headline: IRGC spokesman Hossein Mohebbi says 7 undersea data cables beneath the strait 'could become' Iranian targets
dek: Mohebbi: seven major internet cables run beneath Hormuz and 'could become' new Iranian targets — 'We just want them to know that new targets will be unveiled. New weapons will be unveiled.' Vowed to drive 'remnants of US power' out of the region; posted an AI-generated missile image on X.
sources: IRGC spokesman Brig Gen Hossein Mohebbi (Sacred Defense Museum ceremony, IRIB); IRGC political-affairs deputy commander Brig Gen Yadollah Javani (Al Mayadeen, Oct 20); IRGC chief of staff Maj Gen Ali Abdollahi; CENTCOM s
fault_line: Bluff to scare markets — or the one Iranian threat Washington cannot intercept? Is cutting the internet's backbone under Hormuz a realistic asymmetric weapon, or rhetoric for the cameras?

sections.what_happened: Mohebbi: seven major internet cables run beneath Hormuz and 'could become' new Iranian targets — 'We just want them to know that new targets will be unveiled. New weapons will be unveiled.' Vowed to drive 'remnants of US power' out of the region; posted an AI-generated missile image on X. Javani: Iran has technology to strike US bases beyond West Asia; 'vital cables in the Strait of Hormuz will not be safe if our infrastructure is targeted.' Mohebbi (Tuesday): the strait is 'fully closed' to US/Israeli vessels, US warships 700 km away, and US claims oil is being shipped out are 'entirely false' — 'the passage of a few small vessels smuggling oil does not mean the strait is open.' Abdollahi: forces will answer any aggressor with a response 'that makes it regret any reckless action.' COUNTER: Hawkins (CENTCOM, via AJ): 95% of vessels crossed, waterway 'open and safe'; naval blockade in force; IRGC weakened. Rubio: accused Iran of deliberately targeting commercial vessels, comparing tactics to 'Nazi submarines'; said oil/energy shipments recovered to 80-100% of prewar levels via US protection. Context: Rezaei (Press TV, early Oct) had already warned cables/data centers/AI facilities could be destroyed if war resumes — 'not yet included among our targets.' Saudi Gazette notes the March drone attacks on AWS infrastructure in UAE/Bahrain as precedent.
sections.what_verified: Mohebbi remarks corroborated across Saudi Gazette, Tehran Telegraph, Türkiye Today, Al Khaleej Today, Muslim Network TV, Newscord (which cites RFE/RL: cables carry SWIFT/cloud/Asia-Europe data; Vietnam.vn). Javani/Abdollahi via Al Mayadeen English. Hawkins via Shafaq/AJ. Social engagement corroborates audience pull (RVCJ Media graphic 11K likes Oct 20; BBC Persian fact-check segment 5.2K/400; MeidasTouch 'Iran reveals its next target' 5.2K/500; TRT-style explainer reel 73K/6.3K on Hormuz tonight; Cooper CENTCOM briefing 36K/4.7K Oct 16).
sections.what_disputed: Mohebbi's 'all internet and commercial data traffic passes through them' is IRGC-only — Tehran Telegraph flags this; TeleGeography's verified stat is 90%+ of Europe-Asia capacity through the RED SEA, not Hormuz specifically (claim overstated). The open-vs-closed data war is unresolved: 95%/400-ships/100M-barrels (CENTCOM) vs 'fully closed'/700km (IRGC) — neither publishes full ship-tracking; needs Kpler/LSEG anchor. Mohebbi's missile X-image is AI-generated, noted by IBTimes UK. No cable cut or cable attack has actually occurred.
sections.why_matters: The war's new front is the internet's backbone: Iran's 'new targets, new weapons' doctrine names the cables Washington never mentions. Map-spine Short — Hormuz + the 7 cables + the two incompatible data claims (CENTCOM's 95%/400-ships vs IRGC's fully-closed/700km) with named sources on every beat; TeleGeography's Red Sea correction as the honest data card. From Iran's framing: the cheap-weapons doctrine moves from ships to the digital spine.
sections.context: Background: Hormuz — NEW escalation dimension: IRGC spokesman Hossein Mohebbi says 7 undersea data cables beneath the strait 'could become' Iranian targets; Javani warns cables 'will not be safe' if Iran attacked and says Iran can strike US bases beyond the region; Mohebbi rejects CENTCOM's 'open strait' data as 'entirely false'
